paper.title_en: Hydrodynamic analogue of deformed Lorentz symmetry
paper.abstract_en: Phonons in a class of viscoelastic fluids have been shown to obey modified dispersion relations analogous to those arising in doubly special relativity (DSR). Here, we extend this analogy by demonstrating that these systems admit a deformed Lorentz symmetry, whose generators, together with translations (and rotations in higher dimensions), define a polynomial deformation of the Poincaré algebra. A time-dependent, nonlocal, unitary transformation maps the phonon dynamics to an auxiliary field of Bogoliubov quasiparticles, in which the boost generator and the associated finite transformation can be constructed exactly by integrating the corresponding flow equations. Mapping the symmetry back to the original phonon variables, the corresponding infinitesimal boost generator remains a finite-order local differential operator. While the analogy does not straightforwardly extend to multiparticle sectors it nevertheless provides a concrete physical setting for exploring aspects of DSR phenomenology, such as the inequivalence of kinematical and spectral gamma factors.
